### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.1, the motivating free-monoid adjunction — printed
pp. 213–214, PDF pp. 222–223 (item `awodey:9.1:construction-free-monoid-adjunction`).

Awodey opens Chapter 9 with exactly this construction, but presents it as an
*adjunction*: the underlying-set functor on monoids, the free-monoid functor, the
insertion of generators as unit, and the transposition bijection between monoid
homomorphisms out of the free monoid and functions into the underlying set.
In-tree, `Theory/Algebra/Monoid/Hom.v:83,93` already give the category of monoid
objects and `Mon_Forget`, with no left adjoint; the only formalized instance of
the paradigm is the free *category* on a quiver
(`Construction/Free/Quiver.v:518,550`), of which the free monoid is the
one-object case — asserted in `Construction/Free.v:92` prose but not proved.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.1) Package the free-monoid construction as an `Adjunction`
      (`Theory/Adjunction.v:130`) with `Mon_Forget` as right adjoint and the
      insertion of generators as unit, e.g. through
      `Theory/Universal/Arrow.v:158,214` in the style of
      `Construction/Free/Quiver.v`
- [ ] (from Awodey §9.1) Prove the transposition formula for this instance —
      `Theory/Adjunction.v:264` `to_adj_unit` supplies it once the adjunction
      exists

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.9, Exercise 2 — printed p. 262, PDF p. 271
(item `awodey:9:ex2`).

The exercise draws the standard corollary of the free/forgetful adjunction:
every monoid is a quotient of a free one, the quotient map being the counit at
that monoid. Nothing in-tree says any counit is epic or surjective
(`Theory/Adjunction.v:311` `adj_monic` is the mono-side statement and has no epi
counterpart).

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.9 Ex 2) Prove that the counit of the free/forgetful
      adjunction on monoids is a (split) epimorphism, so every monoid is a
      quotient of a free monoid

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.2, Corollary 9.5 — printed pp. 222–223, PDF
pp. 231–232 (item `awodey:9.2:cor5`).

This is the counit form of the adjunction, obtained by duality: a counit whose
components are couniversal arrows is interchangeable with the natural hom-set
bijection. The library already has the (1) ⇒ (2) leg at full strength —
`Theory/Adjunction.v:248` `adj_univ_impl` (`f ≈ ε ∘ fmap[F] g ↔ ⌊f⌋ ≈ g`),
`:272` `from_adj_counit`, `counit := ⌈id⌉` at `:215`, and
`Adjunction/Opposite.v:34` `Opposite_Adjunction` as the duality tool — but the
(2) ⇒ (1) leg cannot be cited, because `Theory/Universal/Arrow.v` has no dual:
there is no class of couniversal arrows (terminal objects of `F ↓ =(d)`), no
right-adjoint-from-couniversal-arrows constructor, and no assembly theorem. The
dual notion exists only as prose at `Theory/Universal/Arrow.v:23–24`.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.2) Add the dual of `Theory/Universal/Arrow.v`: a
      couniversal-arrow class (terminal object of `F ↓ =(d)`), the
      right-adjoint-from-couniversal-arrows functor, and the adjunction
      assembly — a one-line dualization through `Opposite_Adjunction` if the
      opposite bookkeeping is set up first
- [ ] (from Awodey §9.2) Prove that from `F ⊣ U` each counit component *is* a
      couniversal arrow packaged as such, not merely that the equational form
      `adj_univ_impl` holds

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.3, Example 9.7 — printed pp. 223–224, PDF
pp. 232–233 (item `awodey:9.3:example7`).

Awodey states the same adjunction in Chapter 9 and draws from it the
identification "exponentials are exactly the right adjoints to product
functors". In-tree the hom-set bijection and its naturality equations exist
(`Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v:43,51` `Closed`/`exp_iso`, `:165` `curry_comp_l`,
`:177` `curry_comp`; the full `∃!` universal property at
`Structure/Monoidal/Closed.v:66`), but *neither endpoint is a functor*: there is
no product-with-a-fixed-object functor and no exponential functor `(−)^A`
(`Functor/Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v` defines `ClosedFunctor`, a functor
*preserving* closed structure, which is a different thing), and no `Adjunction`
instance exists for the transpose.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.3) State the identification in both directions: a right
      adjoint to a product functor *is* an exponential, and an exponential gives
      such a right adjoint

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.3, Example 9.8 — printed p. 224, PDF p. 233
(item `awodey:9.3:example8`).

The degenerate index case of the same theorem: a right adjoint to the unique
functor into the terminal category is a terminal object, and dually a left
adjoint is an initial object. In-tree the terminal object and its universal
property are fully formalized (`Structure/Terminal.v:107`), the functor into the
terminal category exists (`Instance/One.v:47` `Erase`), and
`Structure/Limit/Terminal.v:33` proves the genuine biconditional
`Limit F ↔ @Terminal C` for the empty diagram — but *in limit form*. The bridge
from that to the adjoint statement is itself unformalized: no in-tree lemma
identifies the functor category on the empty category with the terminal
category, there is no functor from the terminal category picking out a terminal
object, and no adjunction has `Erase` as an endpoint in either direction.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.3) Prove `C` has a terminal object iff `Erase C : C ⟶ 1`
      has a right adjoint (and dually for initial objects and a left adjoint),
      including the identification of `[0, C]` with the terminal category that
      the argument needs

### Also covered by

diagonal — printed p. 225, PDF p. 234

the product adjunction at `C^op` plus `Adjunction/Opposite.v:34`
`Opposite_Adjunction` gives the statement modulo identifying
`(C^op ∏ C^op)^op` with `C ∏ C`.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.3) Build the internal binary-coproduct bifunctor

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.3, limits and colimits as adjoints to the
constant-diagram functor — printed pp. 225–226, PDF pp. 234–235
(item `awodey:9.3:construction-limit-colimit-adjoints`).

Awodey states the sandwich for a general small index category and adds the
biconditional reading: the left (right) adjoint exists exactly when the ambient
category has all colimits (limits) of that shape. In-tree the sandwich is
available only in Kan-extension clothing and only as a *hypothesis*:
`Theory/Kan/Extension.v:140,222` package `Induced ⊣ Ran` and `Lan ⊣ Induced` as
class fields with no instance anywhere, and they are stated over the
restriction functor along the terminal functor rather than over
`Functor/Diagonal.v:33` `Diagonal J : C ⟶ [J, C]`. There is no limit or colimit
*functor* `[J,C] ⟶ C` at all, and `Structure/Limit/Kan/Extension.v:46`
`Kan_Limit` identifies the right adjoint's value with the limit only object by
object, at a fixed diagram, with no colimit dual.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.3) Construct the limit and colimit functors `[J,C] ⟶ C`
      and state the adjunctions over `Diagonal J`, transporting the
      Kan-extension form across the identification of the functor category on
      the terminal category with the ambient category
- [ ] (from Awodey §9.3) State the biconditional: `Diagonal J` has a right
      (left) adjoint iff the category is `J`-complete (`J`-cocomplete)
- [ ] (from Awodey §9.3) Add the colimit dual of `Kan_Limit`, and upgrade the

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.3, Example 9.10 — printed pp. 226–227, PDF
pp. 235–236 (item `awodey:9.3:example10`).

Awodey presents the polynomial ring as the free *pointed* ring: the forgetful
functor from rings-with-a-distinguished-element to rings has a left adjoint
sending a ring to its polynomial ring with the indeterminate as the point, and
the transposition is evaluation at that point. In-tree there is no ring
structure at all — no ring, rig or semiring in `Theory/Algebra/`
(only monoids, commutative monoids, comonoids and Frobenius objects, all
internal to a monoidal category), no category of rings, no polynomial
construction, and no category of pointed objects to carry the adjunction.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.3) Add the category of pointed rings and the forgetful
      functor to rings
- [ ] (from Awodey §9.3) Prove the polynomial-ring construction is left adjoint
      to it, with the evaluation homomorphism as the transpose

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.4, the definition of an order adjoint / Galois
connection — printed pp. 227–228, PDF pp. 236–237
(item `awodey:9.4:def-order-adjoint-galois`).

Awodey defines an adjunction between preorders as a pair of monotone maps
satisfying the two-way rule, and immediately reads the unit and counit
order-theoretically. Both ingredients are in-tree separately —
`Instance/Proset.v:33` `Proset` makes any preorder a thin category whose
hom-setoid is `equiv _ _ := True`, and `Theory/Adjunction.v:130` `Adjunction` is
the hom-setoid bijection — so an adjunction between two `Proset`s is
*definitionally* the two-way rule and the four naturality fields are trivially
inhabited. What is missing is the specialization itself: there is no
`GaloisConnection` notion, no in-tree constant instantiates `Adjunction` at a
`Proset` or `Poset`, and every occurrence of "Galois connection" in the tree
(`Instance/Poset.v:47,56`, `Theory/Adjunction.v:78`, `Adjunction/GAFT.v:136`,
`Structure/Factorization.v:69`, `Instance/Adjoints.v:280`) is header prose.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.4) State the order-theoretic reading of the unit and
      counit: the unit exhibits the composite at `p` as least among the images
      of the right adjoint above `p`, and dually the counit as greatest

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.4, Example 9.12 (first leg) — printed pp. 228–229,
PDF pp. 237–238 (item `awodey:9.4:example12`; this item is multi-part, and the
dual-image leg is recorded against the quantifiers-as-adjoints issue).

Awodey states the powerset adjoint triple for a function of sets, of which this
issue's obligation is the left half: direct image is left adjoint to inverse
image, `im(f)(U) ⊆ V` iff `U ⊆ f⁻¹(V)`. In-tree only a generalized *middle*
functor exists — `Theory/Subobject/Functor.v:180` `Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets` with
`fmap` given by chosen-pullback reindexing (`:35` `sub_reindex`, functorial via
`:143` `sub_reindex_id`/`sub_reindex_comp`) — and it is valued in `Sets`, not in
a poset category, so it is not even asserted to be monotone for the factorization
preorder of `Theory/Subobject.v:93`. Images exist only as the epi-mono
factorization of a single map (`Instance/Sets/Image.v:143`), never as an induced
operation on subobjects. Nearest relative: `Construction/Slice/Pullback.v:50,67`
gives the slice-level post-composition and pullback functors, with the adjunction
between them only a commented-out stub at lines 121–127.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.4) Prove the topological caveat the example draws:
      restricted to open sets along a continuous map, inverse image keeps its
      right adjoint but loses its left one

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.4, Example 9.12 (second leg) — printed pp. 228–229,
PDF pp. 237–238 (item `awodey:9.4:example12`; multi-part — the direct-image leg
is recorded against the powerset direct-image/inverse-image issue).

Awodey's Example 9.12 states the *triple* `im(f) ⊣ f⁻¹ ⊣ f_*`, the right-hand

powerset-level universal quantifier that this issue covers. In-tree the dual
image has no counterpart of any kind: searches for a dual-image or
universal-image operation return nothing, and the only `Pow` in the tree
(`Structure/Topos.v:129`) is an internal power object with no adjoints.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.4) Give the explicit dual-image formula and prove the
      second adjunction `f⁻¹ ⊣ f_*`, so the whole triple is available at the
      powerset level

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.4, Example 9.13 — printed pp. 229–230, PDF
pp. 238–239 (item `awodey:9.4:example13`; multi-part — the completeness claim is
recorded against the IPC-calculus issue).

Awodey presents the whole propositional structure of a Heyting algebra as
adjoint two-way rules: meets, joins, Heyting implication as an exponential, and
the bounds. The four rules are in-tree as universal properties that degenerate
exactly to Awodey's bi-implications in a thin category, and
`Instance/Props.v:53,61,69,80,94` instantiates all of them for propositions under
entailment (`Props_Terminal`, `Props_Initial`, `Props_Cartesian`,
`Props_Cocartesian`, `Props_Closed`, the last over the live cartesian-closed
class of `Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v`, not the `Structure/Closed.v` stub).
What is missing is the abstract structure and negation: there is no named
Heyting-algebra notion, and no logical negation object anywhere (the "negation"
hits in the tree are `Structure/Additive.v`'s additive-group negation).

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.4) Present the four structural rules uniformly as
      adjunctions at the propositions instance, so the example's "everything is
      an adjoint" reading is visible in the code and not only in prose
- [ ] (from Awodey §9.4) Derive contraposition (from an entailment into a
      negation, infer the swapped entailment) and record the classical extension
      as a separate, opt-in assumption

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.6, the remark on strings of adjoints — printed
pp. 234–235, PDF pp. 243–244 (item `awodey:9.6:remark-adjoint-strings`).

Awodey's illustration is the four-term string between categories and sets:
connected components, the discrete-category functor, the objects functor, and
the codiscrete-category functor. In-tree nothing of it exists: there is no
functor from categories to sets and none back (`rg 'Cat ⟶ Sets'` and the
converse are empty), `Instance/Discrete.v:37,52` gives a `Category`-valued
function and a functor *out of* a discrete category — its own comment at line 31
conceding this is only "the left adjoint at the level of a single witness" —
and `Structure/Discrete.v:23–24` describes the codiscrete right adjoint in prose
only. Every "adjoint string"/"adjoint triple" hit in the tree (six of them,
including `Construction/Arrow.v:61–62`) is a comment; note that
`Adjunction/Compose.v:173` `Adjunction_Compose` is *series* composition, a
different operation.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.6) Add the connected-components leg, so the string has all
      four terms rather than three
- [ ] (from Awodey §9.6) Introduce a name for a string of successive adjoints
      (distinct from `Adjunction_Compose`), so a chain can be stated as one
      object rather than as separate adjunctions

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.6, the distributivity consequences of limit
preservation — printed p. 236, PDF p. 245
(item `awodey:9.6:remark-rapl-distributivity`; multi-part — the quantifier legs
are recorded against the quantifiers-as-adjoints issue).

Awodey's point is that because a product functor is a left adjoint it preserves
*all* colimits, giving the indexed distributivity law. In-tree the law is proved
only in its finite cases and *directly*, not via the adjunction:
`Structure/BiCCC.v:90` `prod_coprod_r` and `:257` `BiCCC_Distributive` give the
binary/nullary distributive isomorphisms, and
`Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v:310` `exp_prod_r` gives the exponential-side law.
The general law is not derivable in-tree, because the product-exponential
adjunction is never packaged as an `Adjunction` object, so
`Adjunction/Continuity.v:223` `left_adjoint_preserves_colimits` cannot be applied
to it.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.6) Once the product functor is an `Adjunction`, derive the
      indexed distributivity law by applying the general cocontinuity theorem,
      and relate it to the existing finite instances

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.6, the quantifier consequences of limit
preservation — printed p. 236, PDF p. 245
(item `awodey:9.6:remark-rapl-distributivity`; multi-part — the distributivity
leg is recorded against the product-functor-as-left-adjoint issue).

Awodey specializes the preservation principle to the quantifier triple: the
universal quantifier preserves meets and the existential preserves joins, and
contrapositively the existential cannot be a right adjoint nor the universal a
left adjoint. Nothing of this exists in-tree, since quantifiers as adjoints are
not formalized at all.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.6) Derive that the universal quantifier preserves meets
      and the existential preserves joins, as corollaries of the adjunctions
      rather than as independent calculations
- [ ] (from Awodey §9.6) Record the contrapositive non-existence readings (the
      existential is not a right adjoint; the universal is not a left adjoint)

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.6, limit preservation as a test for the
(non-)existence of adjoints — printed p. 237, PDF p. 246
(item `awodey:9.6:remark-adjoint-existence-tests`).

Awodey uses the preservation theorem in the negative direction — a functor that
fails to preserve limits (or colimits) can have no adjoint on the relevant side —
and illustrates it with concrete forgetful and free functors. The general tool is
in-tree (`Adjunction/Continuity.v:202,223`) but is **never used in the negative
direction**: `rg 'no left adjoint|has no adjoint|cannot be a right adjoint|fails
to preserve'` returns nothing. Neither of the remark's concrete instances is
available either: there is no category of posets with its forgetful functor, and
no free-monoid functor (`Theory/Algebra/Monoid/Hom.v:93` and
`Instance/CMon.v:169` give forgetful functors with no left adjoints; the tree's
only free/forgetful adjunction is for categories on quivers, and no preservation
consequence is drawn from it).

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.6) State the reusable corollary that a left adjoint
      preserves binary coproducts (and a right adjoint binary products), so the
      test can be applied without unfolding the general colimit machinery each
      time

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.6, Proposition 9.16 — printed pp. 237–239, PDF
pp. 246–248 (item `awodey:9.6:prop16`).

Awodey restates and proves the universal property of the Yoneda embedding in
Chapter 9: every functor from a small category into a cocomplete category
extends along the embedding to a colimit-preserving functor, uniquely up to
isomorphism, the extension being left adjoint to the restricted-hom functor.
In-tree `Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v` provides only the Yoneda lemma and full
faithfulness of the embedding; there is no universal property of the embedding,
no cocontinuous extension, and no adjunction between the extension and the
restriction. Two proof *ingredients* do exist and should be reused rather than
rebuilt: `Theory/Coend/Yoneda.v:174` `coyoneda_reduction` is the density formula
in coend clothing (the tree spells it "co-Yoneda"/"ninja", which is why searches
for "density" miss it), and `Theory/Profunctor.v:155` `Repr_left` is the
right-hand functor in uncurried, bifunctor form.

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.6, Corollary 9.17 — printed p. 239, PDF
pp. 248–250 (item `awodey:9.6:cor17`).

Awodey derives from the free-cocompletion property that precomposition between
presheaf categories has both a left and a right adjoint. The restriction functor
is in-tree in full generality (`Theory/Kan/Extension.v:127` `Induced`), and the
two adjoints are *stated* as class fields (`:140` `RightKan` with
`ran_adjoint : Induced ⊣ Ran`, `:222` `LeftKan` with
`lan_adjoint : Lan ⊣ Induced`), but **neither class has an instance anywhere in
the tree** — the only consumer,
`Structure/Limit/Kan/Extension.v:46` `Kan_Limit`, also takes one as a hypothesis.
So the corollary's entire content (that the adjoints *exist*) is missing, in the
sharpest "definition without required API" form.

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.6) Prove the Yoneda compatibility the corollary adds: the
      left adjoint composed with the Yoneda embedding of the source is naturally
      isomorphic to the Yoneda embedding of the target composed with the functor

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.6, the remark that every functor has an adjoint
into the free cocompletion — printed p. 241, PDF p. 250
(item `awodey:9.6:remark-every-functor-has-adjoint`).

Read backwards, Corollary 9.17 says every functor of small categories has a
presheaf-valued "adjoint", with the caveat that an honest adjoint into the
target category exists exactly when those presheaves are representable — which
is this issue's criterion. In-tree the object exists but nothing is claimed of
it: `Theory/Profunctor.v:155` `Repr_left F := Hom D ◯ (F^op ∏⟶ Id)` is precisely
the composite the remark builds, only uncurried as a bifunctor, and
`Theory/Profunctor/Adjunction.v:70` `representable_adjunction` states the
hom-profunctor form of the criterion but quantifies over an *already given* right
adjoint. `Functor/Representable.v:46` `Representable` exists but has no consumers
anywhere in the tree (no file even imports it).

- [ ] (from Awodey §9.6) Curry the hom-profunctor into a functor from the target
      category into presheaves on the source, so the remark's object can be
      stated in the form Awodey uses (the tree currently has no
      hom-tensor currying for functor categories)
- [ ] (from Awodey §9.6) State the criterion existentially — an adjoint exists
      iff each of those presheaves is representable — rather than only for a
      given adjoint

### Also covered by


Awodey, *Category Theory*, §9.7, Proposition 9.18 (left-adjoint leg) — printed
p. 243, PDF pp. 252–253 (item `awodey:9.7:prop18`; multi-part — the dependent
product is filed separately as the Awodey 9.7 dependent-product issue, which
